analysis.title: Americas Brokers & Crypto: First quarter of crypto estimate upgrades since 4Q25 EPS; muted retail trading, but favorable fall seasonality ahead
key_insights: In 3Q26 brokers and crypto stocks rose 11% on average, outperforming the S&P 500 by about 5pp, driven mainly by multiple rerating. Digital-asset-skewed names rose 23% vs +7% for traditional retail brokers.

GS raises 2026E/27E/28E revenue across the group by 2%/3%/4% on average and 2027E/28E adj. EPS by a median of 5%/6%. Consensus crypto estimates inflect positively for the first time since 4Q25, and GS is more constructive on crypto companies.

Industry retail equity trading volumes were roughly flat MoM in September after 15% declines in July and August. 3Q26 volumes underperformed historical seasonality by 2pp/12pp/14pp in Jul/Aug/Sep. The GS proxy rose 1% sequentially in September and 3% MoM so far in October.

Structural broker growth remains healthy. Platform balances rose 7% and accounts 1% in August across brokers. Margin balances rose 3% industry-wide and 2% across brokers in August, which GS treats as a positive lagged indicator for retail volumes.

Removal of the Pattern Day Trader designation (effective June 4) cut the minimum margin equity from $25,000 to $2,000 and removed the 3-trade limit per 5 days. Retail 0DTE options volume rose 23% MoM in June and 130% YoY. Brokers with smaller average accounts (HOOD) benefited most, and HOOD options volumes kept outperforming the industry in July and August.
Upside optionality exists if large-cap IPOs with retail appeal reaccelerate, supporting account growth, trading, margin lending, securities lending and IPO access fees.

Industry crypto volumes inflected sharply in mid-August after the SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets. In the following month volumes rose 84% MoM, with the 11th-25th largest assets up 138% vs 53% for Bitcoin. DEX volumes rose 107% vs 81% for centralized exchanges.

Crypto volumes remain well below 1H26 and 2025 levels (CEX T7D ADV $26.3bn in 3Q26 average vs $56.9bn in the 2025 average), implying room for further recovery. Perpetual funding rates rose in 3Q26, signaling more bullish positioning.
HOOD's Robinhood App crypto volumes have historically shown the strongest correlation with long-tail crypto volumes, so HOOD is seen as best positioned to benefit from the recent long-tail rebound.

Recent rule changes disproportionately affect less-scaled assets and platforms: the SEC Regulation Crypto Assets proposal (offerings up to $5mn / $75mn), the SEC innovation exemption for tokenized securities venues using automated market makers with volume caps, and the CFTC no-action position on self-custody wallet and DeFi developers.

Crypto estimates stabilized after 2026 estimates fell about 40% in 1H26. Crypto market cap rose 20% and 9%, and volumes rose 16% and 32% MoM, in August and September. Consensus 2026E crypto revenue is trending up while 2027E/28E have stabilized.
The market-implied forward rate curve now embeds about 3.5 additional Fed funds hikes through year-end 2027 vs prior GS model assumptions, which benefits net interest income at HOOD, IBKR and COIN.
Normalizing crypto volumes and balances to mid-cycle levels implies median upside of about 3%/3%/4% to 2027E revenue/adj. EBITDA/adj. EPS, with COIN and HOOD showing the largest uplifts.

Normalized blockchain gas revenue is immaterial, about 0.5% of 2027E total revenue across covered names. The Robinhood Chain peaked at about $8mn of daily gross gas fees in early September, but fee rates have since normalized, and L2 economics are cut by revenue sharing (about 55% of gross fees in the illustrative model).

GS Payments research sizes about $2.6tn of near-term addressable agentic commerce spend and $21.3tn over 7+ years. Agentic activity on blockchains is still nascent, and x402 volumes have fallen from their 4Q25 peak. COIN's x402 handles more than 95% of on-chain agentic transactions, and nearly all settle in CRCL's USDC.

Valuation: digital-asset-skewed firms trade below the 5th percentile of their 5-year multiple range, while retail brokers trade at about 21.5x Q5-Q8 P/E (about the 65th percentile). The group trades at about 21.0x P/E and 12.5x EV/EBITDA on GSe, around the 10th and 20th percentile.

GS favors HOOD, IBKR (retail trading seasonality and structural growth), COIN, HOOD and IBKR and FIGR (rate-sensitive earnings), COIN (recovering crypto and new products) and HOOD (long-tail crypto exposure).

FIGR: consumer loan marketplace growth above 100% YoY, a 58% 2022-26E revenue CAGR and 31% forecast 2026E-28E. The Kiavi acquisition is 15%/17% accretive to 2027E/28E adj. EBITDA, and the stock trades at about 14.0x adj. Q5-Q8 GSe P/E, the lowest since IPO.

COIN estimates inflected for the first time since 4Q25, with 3Q26E/2026E/27E/28E adj. EPS (ex. SBC) up 24%/35%/10%/9%. COIN has gained about 8pp of crypto derivatives share since 1Q24 and trades at about 25.5x Q5-Q8 adj. P/E, around the 5th percentile of its history.
3Q26 GSe vs consensus: GLXY EPS $0.58 vs -$0.05, COIN $2.55 vs $0.18, ETOR $0.33 vs $0.40, CRCL $0.45 vs $0.51, HOOD $0.62 vs $0.62, IBKR $0.64 vs $0.66, FIGR $0.34 vs $0.35, WLTH $0.16 vs $0.15.

market_movers.rationale: PT raised from $219 on an improved crypto backdrop, expense discipline, SEC innovation exemption tailwinds and a trough-level valuation. 3Q26E adj. EPS rises 24% to $2.55.
Best-in-class structural growth from product velocity, plus exposure to a retail trading recovery, long-tail crypto and prediction markets. GS is 2%/3%/4% above 2026E/27E/28E consensus adj. EPS.
Structural account growth (26% 2026E-28E account CAGR vs 8% for peers) and a pre-tax margin above 75%, positioned for a fall retail trading recovery.
Tokenized HELOC growth, accretive Kiavi acquisition and a low valuation of about 14.0x adj. Q5-Q8 P/E. GS is 4%/9%/8% above consensus 2026E/27E/28E adj. EBITDA.
PT cut from $34 and target P/E cut to 7.0x from 8.5x on lower market multiples, while 2027E EPS rises 5%.
PT trimmed from $92 as the target P/E falls to 30.5x from 38.5x, partly offset by 24% higher 2027E EPS.
PT cut from $28 on lower sum-of-the-parts multiples for digital assets and data centers.
PT raised from $7.25 even as the target EV/EBITDA multiple falls to 13.0x from 13.5x.
PT raised from $4.00 with the multiple unchanged at 3.5x EV/gross profit.
PT of $11 is based on 13.5x Q5-Q8 adj. P/E.

sector_views.rationale: Cautiously constructive. Crypto-skewed firms look attractive at below-5th-percentile multiples, while retail brokers are closer to fair value.

earnings_insights: GSe 3Q26 EPS vs Street (estimates, not yet reported): COIN $2.55 vs consensus $0.18, GLXY $0.58 vs consensus -$0.05, BTGO $1.07 vs $0.15, HOOD $0.62 vs $0.62, IBKR $0.64 vs $0.66, FIGR $0.34 vs $0.35, CRCL $0.45 vs $0.51, ETOR $0.33 vs $0.40, WLTH $0.16 vs $0.15, GEMI -$0.19 vs -$0.32. The median EPS gap vs Street is -2%.

GSe 3Q26 adj. EBITDA vs consensus: GLXY $359.9mn vs $72.5mn, COIN $327.9mn vs $251.0mn (12% better ex. SBC), HOOD $743.7mn vs $746.1mn, IBKR $1,456.1mn vs $1,465.3mn, CRCL $196.2mn vs $206.1mn, ETOR $40.3mn vs $49.5mn, FIGR $134.3mn vs $128.4mn, WLTH $39.3mn vs $36.9mn, GEMI -$9.3mn vs -$31.9mn, BTGO -$2.7mn vs $1.3mn.

GS expects COIN transaction revenue roughly in line with the Street, 3% higher subscription and services revenue and 1% higher total revenue. HOOD revenue is 4% above the Street, with other revenue up 12% and transaction revenue up 7%, partly offset by NII 3% lower.
GS expects CRCL net revenue 4% below the Street on 4% lower reserve income, and ETOR total net contribution 5% below the Street.
FIGR consumer loan marketplace volume is tracking above 100% YoY growth in 3Q26, with the 3Q26 GS estimate of about $5.2bn.

Estimate revisions are bifurcated: crypto-exposed firms (COIN, HOOD, GLXY) see upgrades, while a muted retail trading backdrop drives downgrades for retail brokers. Median 2027E/28E EPS rises 5%/6%, and the median 12-month PT is largely unchanged with a median total upside of 10%.
Hypothetical mid-cycle crypto normalization implies 2027E adj. EPS uplift of 13% for COIN, 5% for HOOD, 4% for BTGO, 3% for ETOR, 11% for GLXY and 2% for GEMI.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A higher forward rate curve than GS previously modeled raises net interest income at rate-sensitive HOOD, IBKR and COIN.
Retail trading volumes were roughly flat MoM in September but remain far below last year, weighing on retail broker estimates.

macro_indicators.reading: $1,454bn in August 2026, up 3% MoM and 37% YoY
macro_indicators.interpretation: Margin balance growth turning positive has historically led retail equity trading volumes with a lag.

crypto_views: Crypto market cap and volumes stabilized in 3Q26: market cap rose 20% and 9% and volumes rose 16% and 32% MoM in August and September. The 4Q25-2Q26 downturn matched or exceeded the historical average sell-off (51% market cap and 66% volume declines).

SEC proposed Regulation Crypto Assets on Aug. 18, and the SEC innovation exemption and CFTC no-action position followed on Sept. 17. The reforms mostly help smaller digital assets and venues, and DEXs are still under 20% of spot volumes.
Long-tail crypto assets recovered faster than Bitcoin: 138% volume growth in the 11th-25th largest assets vs 53% for Bitcoin in the month after the proposal.
Perpetual futures funding rates rose in 3Q26 (ann. avg. BTC BTC funding rate 4.62%), signaling more bullish positioning.
COIN integrated Coinbase International Exchange with Deribit, and its derivatives share has risen about 8pp since 1Q24. Subscription and services were about 40% of 2025 COIN revenue.

Blockchain gas revenue is immaterial. Chains launched by HOOD (Robinhood Chain), COIN (Base) and CRCL (Arc) grew in accounts and value locked, but gas fees are designed to be low and are expected to fall with competition.
x402 handles more than 95% of on-chain agentic transactions, and nearly all agentic volume settles in USDC (99.6% cumulative).

trade_ideas.description: Buy-rated names into 3Q26 earnings: HOOD, IBKR (retail trading recovery and structural growth), COIN (crypto recovery and new products), FIGR (HELOC growth and rates)
trade_ideas.rationale: Structural growth, favorable fall seasonality, higher-rate beneficiaries and recovering crypto activity, with crypto-skewed valuations at trough multiples.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower retail engagement, faster rate cuts, a crypto market downturn and weaker regulatory progress.

trade_ideas.description: Near-term exposure to long-tail crypto via HOOD
trade_ideas.rationale: Robinhood App crypto volumes correlate most with smaller-asset volumes, which drove the recent crypto inflection.

risk_factors: Retail trading remains muted versus seasonality, with volumes 38% lower YoY in September.
Crypto market volatility and a persistently lower crypto market cap.
Faster-than-expected interest rate cuts would reduce NII at HOOD, IBKR and COIN and HELOC demand at FIGR.
Regulatory risk, including insufficient crypto deregulatory reform and payment-for-order-flow regulation.
Gas-fee competition and revenue sharing could keep blockchain revenue de minimis, and agentic commerce faces adoption barriers (agent authority, liability and data security).
Share loss to USDT, competition from other stablecoins, and Coinbase de-emphasizing USDC (CRCL risk factors).
Slowing AI investment and data center oversupply (GLXY).

tension_points.bull_case: Structural account and asset growth, rising margin balances, PDT removal, favorable fall seasonality and possible IPO recovery should lift retail volumes.
tension_points.bear_case: 3Q26 retail volumes underperformed seasonality by 2pp/12pp/14pp, were down 25%/32%/38% YoY in Jul/Aug/Sep, and retail broker estimates are being cut.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Retail volumes failing to follow historical fall seasonality despite margin balance growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Volumes rose 84% in the month after the SEC proposal and consensus estimates inflected up for the first time since 4Q25.
tension_points.bear_case: Volumes remain well below 1H26 and 2025 levels, and the rebound is concentrated in long-tail assets and unregulated venues.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Crypto market cap trending down over time or a reversal in recent volume momentum.

tension_points.bull_case: HOOD, COIN and CRCL chains are growing users and value locked, and the agentic commerce TAM could reach $21.3tn.
tension_points.bear_case: Normalized gas revenue is about 0.5% of 2027E revenue, fees likely fall with competition, and x402 volumes are down from the 4Q25 peak.
